newsitem.title: INDIA: RBI eases norms for Indian investment in Nepal.
newsitem.headline: RBI eases norms for Indian investment in Nepal.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Monday it relaxed norms for overseas investment by Indians in Nepal.
Proposals for investment in Nepal up to a limit of 250 million Indian rupees would be cleared under the fast track route, the RBI said in a statement.
Unlike other companies coming under this route, proposals for investment in Nepal would not be linked to export/foreign exchange earnings of the applicant company, the RBI said.
The central bank also removed a requirement that investments exceeding $15 million would have to be raised through an issue of global depositary receipts.
"This condition will not apply to rupee investments in Nepal," the RBI said.
The RBI also relaxed its norms on repatriation of returns on investment.
"At present, an Indian promoter company is required to repatriate all its entitlements by way of dividend, royalty, technical know how fees, etcetera, in free foreign exchange," it said.
"The returns on rupee investments in Nepal shall however be allowed to be repatriated in Indian rupees," it said.
All other existing terms and conditions applicable to overseas investment in joint ventures and subsidiaries will continue to apply to investments in Nepal, the RBi said.
